# Compile errors

Every program here is a test in `tests/errors/` and `tests/errors_pkg/` that must fail to compile. The text under "The message contains" is the part of the error that the test checks for, so the full message may add the file, line and a suggested fix. Each is grouped by feature.

- [`do!` blocks](#do-blocks): 7 errors
- [Anonymous struct literals](#anonymous-struct-literals): 4 errors
- [Closures](#closures): 28 errors
- [Comptime and macros](#comptime-and-macros): 28 errors
- [Declarations and parsing](#declarations-and-parsing): 3 errors
- [Error handling](#error-handling): 8 errors
- [Interfaces](#interfaces): 42 errors
- [Optimization attributes](#optimization-attributes): 17 errors
- [Packages and imports](#packages-and-imports): 7 errors
- [Other](#other): 45 errors

## `do!` blocks

### do after call

The message contains:

```text
do! would run before 'side()', which comes first in the statement
```

This program fails to compile:

```odin
package main
side :: proc() -> int { return 1 }
main :: proc() {
	n := side() + do! { take 1 }
	_ = n
}
```

### do in defer

The message contains:

```text
do! can only be used in a declaration, an assignment, an expression statement or a return
```

This program fails to compile:

```odin
package main
import "core:fmt"
main :: proc() {
	defer fmt.println(do! { take 1 })
}
```

### do no take

The message contains:

```text
do!: the block needs a 'take value'
```

This program fails to compile:

```odin
package main
main :: proc() {
	x := do! { y := 1; _ = y }
	_ = x
}
```

### do short circuit

The message contains:

```text
do! would run before the statement, even when the right side of '&&' is skipped
```

This program fails to compile:

```odin
package main
main :: proc() {
	ready := false
	ok := ready && do! { take true }
	_ = ok
}
```

### do take in nested proc

The message contains:

```text
'take' gives the value of a do! { ... } or comptime! { ... } block, and cannot be used in a proc nested inside it
```

This program fails to compile:

```odin
package main
main :: proc() {
	n := do! {
		f := proc() -> int { take 1 }
		take f()
	}
	_ = n
}
```

### do ternary branch

The message contains:

```text
do! would run before the statement, even when its branch of the ternary is not taken
```

This program fails to compile:

```odin
package main
main :: proc() {
	n := 1 if true else do! { take 2 }
	_ = n
}
```

### do two values

The message contains:

```text
do!: 'take' takes exactly one value
```

This program fails to compile:

```odin
package main
main :: proc() {
	x := do! { take 1, 2 }
	_ = x
}
```

### closure ref passed chain

The message contains:

```text
this closure captures &n and is passed to later (line 17), where it is passed to keep (line 11), where it is appended to memory behind a pointer (line 7)
```

This program fails to compile:

```odin
package main

Handlers :: struct { all: [dynamic]closure() }

keep :: proc(hs: ^Handlers, f: closure()) {
	append(&hs.all, f)
}

later :: proc(hs: ^Handlers, f: closure()) {
	keep(hs, f)
}

register :: proc(hs: ^Handlers) {
	n := 0
	g := proc[&n]() { n += 1 }
	later(hs, g)
}

main :: proc() {
	hs: Handlers
	register(&hs)
}
```

```odin
make_scaler :: proc!(T: Type) -> Expr {

	return quote(1)
}
main :: proc() { _ = make_scaler!(string) }
```

## Error handling

### catch must leave scope

The message contains:

```text
a 'catch' block after a declaration or assignment must leave the scope
```

This program fails to compile:

```odin
package main
Error :: enum { None, Bad }
f :: proc() -> (int, Error) { return 1, .None }
main :: proc() {
	x := f() catch err {
		_ = err
	}
}
```

### catch on compound assign

The message contains:

```text
'catch' goes after a call
```

This program fails to compile:

```odin
package main
Error :: enum { None, Bad }
f :: proc() -> (int, Error) { return 1, .None }
main :: proc() {
	x := 0
	x += f() catch unreachable
}
```

### catch typed decl

The message contains:

```text

```

This program fails to compile:

```odin
package main

main :: proc() {
	x: int = f() catch unreachable
}
```
